subject.title: Per-account native command prefix for multi-agent slash commands

question: Should Slack multi-account native slash commands be solved with explicit account-level `nativeNames`, constrained `nativePrefix` sugar, or documented as unsupported for duplicate native command names?
rationale: The current code lacks the account naming boundary, and the two closed implementation attempts show a real design fork that expands Slack config/API surface either way.

options.title: Implement validated nativeNames
options.body: Add explicit per-account native-name mapping with format/collision validation, registration and reverse lookup support, arg-menu roundtrip coverage, docs, and tests.

options.title: Implement constrained nativePrefix
options.body: Add prefix sugar with strict lowercase slug validation and no broad dash-stripping fallback, accepting simpler setup at the cost of another naming abstraction.

options.title: Document unsupported duplicate names
options.body: Keep runtime unchanged and document that multiple Slack apps in one workspace must not register identical native slash command names.

recommendation.title: Implement validated nativeNames
recommendation.body: Add explicit per-account native-name mapping with format/collision validation, registration and reverse lookup support, arg-menu roundtrip coverage, docs, and tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current-code and history evidence for the Slack native-command registry and config surface points to steipete.
